newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: SOCCER-JUVENTUS LOSE 100 PER CENT RECORD AFTER DRAW IN VIENNA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-JUVENTUS LOSE 100 PER CENT RECORD AFTER DRAW IN VIENNA.

text.p: European champions Juventus were held to a surprise 1-1 draw by Rapid Vienna in an action-packed Champions' League Group C match which cost the Italians their first points of the competition on Wednesday.

Athought Juventus lead the group with seven points from three games after beating Manchester United and Fenerbahce, their lead at the top was cut to just one point following United's 2-0 win over Fenerbahce in Istanbul.
And despite his team failing to win for the second time in four days following a 2-1 loss to Vicenza in an Italian League match last Sunday, Juve coach Marcello Lippi was not too unhappy.
"I'm happy with the result but we could have got more out of it," he said.

"We should have made better use of our chances and opportunities, especially from those deep balls. But we gave our best and we tried to play high quality soccer, but all we got out of it was a draw."
Juventus were visibly weakened by the absence of goalkeeper Angelo Peruzzi, midfielder Antonio Conte and forward Alessandro Del Piero but took the lead in the ninth minute.
Christian Vieri profited from a mistake by Rapid's Polish forward Andrzej Lesiak to score after a cross from Croatian striker Alen Boksic.

Rapid coach Ernst Dokupil, considered taking Lesiak off after that and told Prvoslav Jovanovic to warm-up and get ready to replace him, but Lesiak, replied with an equalizer in the 20th minute and kept his place on the pitch.
The goal was a stunner -- a 20-metre free-kick which thundered through the Juventus defensive wall and into the net.

Vladimir Jugovic missed an opportunity to give Juventus victory in the 84th minute when he found himself unmarked in front of the Rapid goal, but his poor shot hit the outside of the post and bounced away.
Dokupil was pleased with his team, who maintained their long unbeaten home record in Europe.
"Juventus had the better chances but we stood up to the pressure. The longer the match went on the more opportunities we had," he said. "But I guess we have to be satisfied with one point."

Rapid Vienna - 1-Michael Konsel, 4-Trifon Ivanov, 5-Peter Schoettel, 6-Peter Stoeger, 7-Christian Stumpf, 10-Didi Kuehbauer, 11-Christian Prosenik, 15-Andrzej Lesiak, 17-Rene Wagner (18-Sergej Mandreko 69), 19-Thomas Zingler, 20-Andreas Heraf
